messages.subject: Highly correlated posterior predictive samples in time series prediction
parts:
Hi, 

I am using R-INLA for time series prediction and noticed that the posterior predictive samples can be highly correlated. 

Here is a simple example illustrating the problem: https://sieste.github.io/inla-project/sampler-problem and I also attach the key figure that nicely illustrates the problem.

Are there any options I can set in `control.compute` or in `inla.posterior.sample` to improve the behavior of the sampler?

Hi,
You may be seeing the effect of the simplified way in which inla.posterior.sample handles the hyperparameters, theta. It only generates theta from the set of integration points of the inla method.  This means that the latent variables are sampled conditionally on those theta values. Normally though, the distributions are highly overlapping, making this effect non-noticeable.

One can use a different function for more fully sampling from the posterior for theta, but those samples can’t automatically be used for latent variable sampling without extra work.

The most straightforward solution is instead to increase the number of integration points. I don’t have my laptop handy to check, but my best bet is to have a look at
  ?control.inla
For how to increase the number of integration points.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Highly correlated posterior predictive samples in time series prediction
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply, Finn. I didn't have any luck with `control.inla`, but then I also didn't try very hard.

However, I think I was able to narrow the problem down a bit further. There seems to be a bug related to the `seed` argument in `inla.posterior.samples`. If I do not specify the seed, the strong correlation between posterior samples disappears. I updated the example at https://sieste.github.io/inla-project/sampler-problem and attached the updated figure as well.
